reviews.overall: The game can't be finished by honest play yet. The `hire_miner` pad sits inside the `mine_entrance` collision circle, so step 8 of 11 can never be paid. Separately, the customer market dies around minute 9–10: departing villagers never despawn, pile up at the map's bottom edge, and trap newly spawned customers. On top of that, two independent softlocks are easy to hit naturally: a customer who got part of their order waits forever for that one food, and raw items in a full bag can't go anywhere. Each of them stopped every honest full run I made. I measured with a bot that steers only via `__FV.setInput`, running a fixed 60 fps simulation about 20–30x faster than real time. With those bugs worked around in memory only (no files edited), pacing is roughly on target: the optimal bot completes the village in 13.9 min, and a casual-human model (about 1.2 s pause between actions, 85% joystick) takes 22.1 min, so I estimate 25–30 min for a real first-timer. Beats come every 0.5–1.8 min, and there are no dead moments: the player always has hauling to do. The design weaknesses are that the player carries 100% of finished goods forever (about 85% of playtime is courier work, with no idle income); backpack/boots upgrades make you slower to finish (12.1 min without vs 13.9 min with); and three of the five second-worker pads add zero output. The tutorial arrow is good for the first 30 s, but afterwards it can point at impossible actions, and an arrow-only player got stuck for 27+ minutes. I propose concrete balance.js numbers below (v1): they keep a casual session around 20 min, keep the longest gap between beats near 1.7 min for the optimal bot, and make upgrades pay back.

The build looks close to the reference: the palette matches (blue sea with fish, terracotta plaza, log palisades, white-parka chief, item towers), and the core art pieces hold together. The basics are solid. The 8-direction mirroring is clean (per-frame body centroids sit within ±3 px of the anchor, so W/SW/NW don't jump sideways), feet sit on the soft shadows, and depth sorting against fences, the grill, trees, huts and the lodge is correct. The biggest first-impression problems are three. First, the carried tower hides the chief's face whenever he walks toward the camera, which happens on the very first trip from the net to the grill. Second, the canvas always renders at 720 px wide, so on 3x phones everything, text included, is upscaled 1.8x and looks soft. Third, the opening frame is weak: the view is clamped to the top, nearly half the screen is empty floor, and the counter and its queue are cut off at the right edge. Next in importance: integration bugs a player will notice. The fisherman's splashes land on snow and on the hut roof. Customer bubbles stack so the front customer's request is the one hidden. The market, trade post and stations never fade, so the chief can vanish behind them. Customers come in only 3 variants (one looks like Santa). Further down the list are the trodden paths, which look like glass tubes, particles that disappear on white snow, a title hero who floats in mid-air, no landscape fallback, and no safe-area handling for the planned Capacitor app. I prototyped tower placements at runtime (no source edits). Putting the tower on the head for all directions (C_all) reads best: the face is always visible, the count stays readable and nothing jumps between directions. A side/behind carry (A2) is the alternative if the arms-at-chest pose must stay.

The basics hold up well in real browser runs. The game starts and plays when localStorage throws on every access. Coins and partial payments are conserved when the page reloads during an unlock payment. Six in-game resets in a row leave listener, timer, texture and sound counts unchanged. Multi-touch ownership, releasing outside the canvas, touchcancel, window blur with a key held and 40 rapid taps all behave. The GPU side is cheap: 4–6 draw calls per frame, and no texture uploads except while a pad's cost text changes. There were 0 console warnings. Four serious problems are confirmed, with the details below. (1) Every customer who buys something never despawns: their last exit waypoint is outside the walkable area. In a 12-minute soak, 132 accumulated and Game update time grew 7×. With 600 injected it reaches 35 ms per frame, so long sessions will grind down. (2) Saves are never validated. Some corrupted fields brick the game with a blank screen that survives every reload; others set coins to NaN or stop the chief moving for good. Any exception inside Phaser's loop freezes the game with no error shown. (3) While the window is blurred but still visible, sound objects pile up (~12/s) and play all at once when focus returns. (4) Payment state and designer edits can cause softlocks: upgrades leave stale "paid" credit after a reload, and a cost of 0 or a lowered cost never completes. Absolute FPS here is not representative: SwiftShader software rendering on 4 shared cores gave 2–4 FPS rendered and 30–50 FPS logic-only. I relied on per-frame logic times and object counts instead.

The game deploys cleanly on both paths. GitHub Pages: no absolute URLs anywhere (index.html, manifest.webmanifest, src, all six asset manifests). The repo root was served under /nurient/ and /nurient/frost-village was opened, including the 301 to the trailing slash. The full loop ran with 0 page or console errors, 0 failed requests, and progress persisted across a reload. The repo is public and Pages is already on, but main only contains privacy.html, so the game appears at https://hyun800115-create.github.io/nurient/frost-village/ only after the branch is merged.

Artifact: I wrote tools/build/build_artifact.mjs. It produces dist/artifact/: a body-only index.html, one esbuild IIFE/ES2019 game.js (32 modules, 0.14 MB), lib/ and assets/. That is 168 files and 14.8 MB. In host emulation it PASSES in four setups: an opaque-origin sandbox iframe with CSP plus CORS, an allow-same-origin frame, standalone, and raw. It boots, renders real art, unlocks audio on the tap, plays the fish→grill→counter→coins loop, has no console errors, and copes with localStorage throwing.

Worst case: an opaque-origin frame whose files come without CORS. There every Phaser XHR is blocked, and then a src bug crashes the Title (finding 1). For that case I added a tested fallback, --inline. It embeds all assets in script packs: 7 files, 12 requests, no XHR, and it PASSES in the strictest emulation. It also runs by double-click from file://.

Payload: a first visit downloads about 11.9 MB, 64% of it PNG. The optional --webp build is tested and looks the same in side-by-side shots, and it cuts this to 8.8 MB. Deferring the in-game music and ambience would take about 2 MB more off the time to the title screen.

I wrote a short Korean README for the designer. No src/, assets/ or index.html was edited. dist/ is still gitignored by frost-village/.gitignore (commit 3b95bba); that is the lead's call.

findings.title: Departing customers never despawn: the market stops selling after ~9 min, and CPU cost and object count grow without limit
findings.repro: node frost-village/tools/test/review_gameplay_market.mjs 15 (keeps 30 grilled fish on the shelf as test setup and lets customers run). Compare: node tools/test/review_gameplay_market.mjs 8 '{"market":{"entry":[[990,2570],[990,1260],[1080,1080]],"exit":[[1080,1080],[990,1260],[990,2570]]}}' _fixed
findings.evidence: Cause: the last exit waypoint (990,2660) is below Collision.resolve's clamp y ≤ H-40 = 2580, and the 'leave' state needs to come within 30 px of it, so a departing customer never despawns. New customers spawn at entry[0] (990,2660→2580), right inside the crowd. Per minute: served 17,19,18,19,17,20,17,11,9,0,0,0,3,7,0. Leaving customers 17→157, agents 22→163, display objects 602→1172, ms/frame 0.28→2.87 (desktop CPU, headless). After ~9 min the front customer is stuck at the spawn point (dSlot≈1776 px). Screenshot /tmp/fv_review/gameplay/market_leaving_crowd.jpg shows ~150 villagers in front of the chief lodge. In the honest smart2 run the shelf stayed frozen at 80 items from 600 s onward. With a reachable exit (y=2570), leaving stays ≤6, ms/frame ~0.1, and 17–19 customers/min are served steadily (market_leaving_crowd_fixed.jpg). The phone frame-time impact is my extrapolation, not measured.
findings.suggested_fix: Set world.js market.entry[0] and exit[last] to y ≤ 2570. In Seller.js Customer 'leave', also despawn when the path is empty or the customer is below y≈2450 and off-camera, or after a stuck timeout. Consider spawning customers off-screen but closer (e.g. (990,1700)) to cut the ~13 s walk.

findings.title: Partly served customer blocks the queue forever; with a bag of unsellable food this becomes a hard softlock
findings.repro: Happened naturally in both honest full runs (bugs GP-01/02 worked around): node tools/test/review_gameplay_sim.mjs --name smart3 --upg greedy --minutes 45 --after 8 --world '{"pads":{"hire_miner":{"x":778,"y":1889}},"market":{"entry":[[990,2570],[990,1260],[1080,1080]],"exit":[[1080,1080],[990,1260],[990,2570]]}}' ; and the same with --name noupg --upg none. Market.update only lets the front customer switch food when got===0 && need===want.count.
findings.evidence: smart3 (just after village complete, ~15.5 min): front customer wants meat x4, got 3, need 1; shelf fish 40 / bread 40 / meat 0 (maxPerType=40 is hard-coded); smokehouse full at 30/36 meat; the player's bag (cap 20) holds 11 fish + 9 bread, so no meat can be picked up. Coins frozen at 636 for the rest of the run. noupg (~9 min): front customer wants fish x2, got 1; shelf bread 40, fish 0; bag holds 6 bread at cap 6; coins frozen at 476 for 36 simulated minutes. Screenshot /tmp/fv_review/gameplay/smart3_999_end.jpg. Recoverable only by reloading the page, because the queue isn't saved.
findings.suggested_fix: In Seller.js Market.update, let the front customer switch to any stocked food whenever theirs runs out (drop the got===0 condition), or complete them with partial payment after ~3 s. Make maxPerType a balance.js value and raise it. Add a universal sink (see GP-04). I applied the first fix in memory (--fixmarket) for all pacing runs, and no further stalls occurred.

findings.title: Raw-item softlock: a bag full of raw items while that station's input AND output are full; persists after reload
findings.repro: node frost-village/tools/test/review_gameplay_softlock.mjs: hire the fisherman (30 coins via give), walk off for 150 s (the grill fills to 30 in / 36 out), stand at the net (auto-gather fills the bag with 6 raw fish), go to the grill input pad ('가득 찼어요!'), go to the output pad ('가방이 가득 찼어요!'), wait 60 s, save, reload.
findings.evidence: After reload: bag = 6× item_fish_raw, grill {in:30,out:36,working:false} → 'SOFTLOCK REPRODUCED (persists across reload)'. A station with a full output stops processing, so its input never frees, and nothing else accepts raw items (market = foods, trade = goods, no discard). All 5 chains share this structure. Auto-gather fires whenever the chief stands still within 78 px of a resource, and the net sits right next to the grill input, so it's easy to trigger by accident. Screenshots /tmp/fv_review/gameplay/softlock_2_grill_output_full_bag_full.jpg, softlock_3_after_reload.jpg.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a universal sink: the trade-post merchant buys anything (raw items for 1 coin, food at half price), or add a trash pad near the plaza. Also skip auto-gathering a resource when its station's input and output are both full.

findings.title: The player must carry every finished good forever; no idle income, ~85% of playtime is courier work
findings.repro: Any honest run, e.g. node tools/test/review_gameplay_sim.mjs --name e1 --upg greedy --minutes 40 --after 10 --fixmarket --world '<GP-01/02 override>'. Look at fin.taskTime in /tmp/fv_review/gameplay/e1_greedy.json.
findings.evidence: e1_greedy (24 min): collect 550 s + sell 666 s out of 1440 s (85%); hand-gathering 31 s in total. smart3 before completion: collect+sell 780 of 840 s. Workers only carry raw → station input (Worker.js 'deliver' → station.inPad). With the player away, every chain stalls within ~1.5–2 min (smart2 at 600 s: grill/sawmill/bakery/smelter all 30/36). The trip from market shelf (1404,835) to smelter output (723,1934) is ~1100 px, about 5–6 s one way at base speed. My Mini Mart and Idle Lumber Inc hand selling and carrying to hired helpers mid-game, and that's the 'idle' payoff. Here the village never earns on its own, so late-game play is a long courier loop.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a porter/cart hire per zone (after its first worker) that moves station output to its seller, plus a cashier at the market. The hire2_* pads could become these porters. Offline earnings can come later. Without code changes, balance.js can only soften this, e.g. faster upgrades.speed.

findings.repro: node tools/test/review_visual_run.mjs /tmp/fv_review/visual/scen/dirs.mjs --vp 430x932 --dpr 3 --fresh (FV_PRINT=1 prints bounds). It renders still Characters in all 8 dirs, empty / 6 items / 12 items. Variants are runtime-patched carryPoints via FV_VARIANTS JSON: A_side, B_back, C_overhead, C_all, A2_side.

So in S the head and face are 100% covered and in SE the face is covered. With 12 items the tower rises above the head but still covers the face. The face then stays visible, the count is readable at any size, turning never jumps, and it echoes the reference's tall salmon tower. In Character.sync, lerp the carry offset over ~100 ms on direction changes. Follow-up: re-render carry_idle/carry_walk with arms raised to touch the bottom item (Blender pipeline is re-runnable). Alternative if the chest pose must stay (A2): S [25,-24,false], SE [-24,-30,false] (far side), E [-14,-46,true]. Avoid pure back-carry (B): 1–4 items vanish behind the head.

findings.title: Canvas renders at 720 px wide regardless of devicePixelRatio, so everything is soft on modern phones
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_visual_run.mjs /tmp/fv_review/visual/scen/crisp.mjs --vp 430x932 --dpr 3 --fresh; compare 1:1 crops crisp_3_hud.jpg / crisp_3_char.jpg
findings.evidence: canvas.width/height = 720x1561 while the device has 1290x2796 px (430x932 CSS @3x), so the browser upscales 1.79x. Text resolution:2 doesn't help because the canvas itself is low-res. HUD digits, Korean objective text and sprite edges are visibly blurry at 1:1. A typical Android phone (412 CSS @2.625 = 1080 px) gets a 1.5x upscale; only DPR-2 iPhones (1.08x) look sharp.
findings.suggested_fix: Render at device resolution. Set the game size to round(720*k) x round(H*k), with k = clamp(cssWidth*dpr/720, 1, 2). Multiply the Game camera zoom by k and give the UI and Title cameras setZoom(k) with origin (0,0), so all layout code keeps its 720-wide logical coordinates (UI.layout divides gameSize by k). Recompute k on resize. Cap k at ~2 for fill-rate.

findings.title: Opening frame is weak: camera clamped to the top, half the screen is empty floor, counter and queue cut off
findings.repro: Fresh start at 390x844 (vp_390x844_2start.jpg, frame_current.jpg). Prototype: /tmp/fv_review/visual/scen/framing.mjs (frame_A_center_loop_z12.jpg, frame_B_center_loop_z135.jpg).
findings.evidence: Visible world height is 1558/1.2 = 1298 px and the camera target is player y 500, so the view clamps to world y=0. The chief sits at ~40% of screen height, the sea fills the top ~29%, and the bottom ~45% is bare plaza floor plus road. The market counter (x=1298) is outside the 635–1235 view: only its awning and the bubbles show at the right edge. The '어부 고용' hire label is clipped at the left edge. Centering the camera on the loop (≈1090,660) shows net, grill, counter, queue and cash pad together.
findings.suggested_fix: While the tutorial runs, frame the core loop instead of the player: add a camera lead or offset toward the counter, or focus on the net/grill/counter centroid until the first sale. Move market_counter inward (e.g. Z('plaza', 1.8, 3.8)) and the hire pad right, so the loop fits in one portrait screen. Put early decor on the empty plaza (crates/barrels, lamp posts, a central brazier or well). Consider zoom 1.3: characters are ~13% of screen width vs ~15% in the reference.

findings.title: Customers who bought food never despawn (exit waypoint is outside the world) → unbounded object/agent growth, O(n²) slowdown
findings.area: performance / unbounded growth (Seller.js Customer, world.js market.exit, Collision.js)
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_robust_soak.mjs 720 --norender: unlockAll, then an in-page bot sells and collects for 12 min of game time. Sample __FV.scene.market.leaving every 30 s. Projection: node tools/test/review_robust_crowd.mjs injects 100/300/600 leaving customers and times the Game update. Root cause: world.js:68 exit ends at [990, 2660], but Collision.resolve clamps y ≤ H−40 = 2580 (Collision.js:74). Customer 'leave' (Seller.js:320-323) needs to get within 30 px of that point, so path.shift()/despawn() never happens.
findings.evidence: Soak (soak_norender_samples.json), 0→739 s of game time: market.leaving 0→132 (~11/min, linear). Every one was at y=2560–2580 with path.length 1. agents 16→148, children 676→1576 (Sprites 42→175; Images 611→1371 because each keeps its carried stack). Game scene update avg 0.57→3.87 ms; whole logic step 1.39→4.53 ms; heap after GC 9.98→11.51 MB. Injection (crowd.json), Game update avg/p95: 0 stuck 0.55/1.2 ms; 100: 2.76/6.7; 300: 10.57/17.3; 600: 35.2/58.6 ms. After 600 more frames all 600 were still stuck at y=2580. Screenshot: /tmp/fv_review/robust/crowd_600_stuck_customers.jpg (wall of customers at the south edge). The rendered soak shows the same trend (leaving 0→11 in ~80 s of game time).
findings.suggested_fix: Put the exit endpoint inside the walkable area (e.g. [990, 2560]). Also despawn when y > H−80, or after a leave timeout (e.g. 8 s) as a safety net. Optionally cap market.leaving and skip agent separation for agents that are off-screen.

findings.title: Save data is not validated: some corrupt fields brick the game permanently (blank screen on every reload), others silently break the session (NaN coins, immobile chief)
findings.repro: Set localStorage['frostVillage.save.v1'] and reload. Run all variants: node tools/test/review_robust_save_fast.mjs. (a) {"v":1,...,"player":{"x":900,"y":1150,"stack":{}}} → tap start. (b) stack: ["item_fish_raw",5,null]. (c) coins: "abc". (d) progress.up: {capacity:-1,speed:-1}, or "x", or 1.5. (e) market.cash: "NaN". (f) player.x: "abc".
findings.evidence: (a) pageerror 'TypeError: sv.player.stack.slice is not a function' at Game.restore (Game.js:721). The Game scene is stuck in CREATING (status 4), the UI never launches and the frame counter stops. After a full reload with the save still present it crashes the same way: a blank pale-blue screen forever (savefast_stackObject_after_reload.jpg). (b) 'TypeError: key.startsWith is not a function' at guessKind (Placeholders.js:397) → same permanent freeze. (c) Economy does Math.max(0, Math.floor('abc')) = NaN. The HUD shows 'NaN', collecting cash leaves coins NaN, and the save writes coins:null, so all coins are lost on the next load. (d) BALANCE values[-1 | 'x' | 1.5] is undefined, so player.speed is NaN, the position becomes NaN/NaN and the chief cannot move or gather (0 items in 240 frames). The bad 'up' values are saved back unchanged, so every session is broken. (e) CashPad.value stays NaN, so every customer payment vanishes for the session. (f) player.x becomes a string that grows by concatenation every frame ('abc1.13378…') and camera scrollX is NaN. Variants that are handled fine: invalid JSON, '', null, an array, v:0/v:2 (fresh start), negative coins, '250', null/off-world position, oversized stacks, stations.i 'abc'/1e9.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sanitize step in Save.load. Use Number.isFinite and Math.floor for coins, cash and positions. Clamp upgrade levels to integers in 0..len-1. Require Array.isArray(stack), filter it to known item keys and cap it to capacity. Check typeof object for done/paid/up/stations/market, and keep only known item types in shelf stock. Wrap Game.create's restore in try/catch: on any exception, copy the raw save to 'frostVillage.save.v1.bad' and start fresh.

findings.title: While the window is blurred (game still visible and running), sfx pile up in a suspended AudioContext and play all at once when focus returns
findings.area: audio / platform (desktop window switching, any iframe embed)
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_robust_audio.mjs only=blur: unlockAll, stand at the plaza, window.dispatchEvent(new Event('blur')), run 900 frames, then dispatch 'focus'. In real use this is clicking another window on desktop, or clicking the host page outside an embedded game iframe.
findings.evidence: Phaser keeps the loop running on blur (TimeStep.blur only changes delta smoothing) but suspends WebAudio (WebAudioSoundManager.onBlur → context.suspend()). Audio.play (Audio.js:36-56) keeps calling sound.play(); each WebAudioSound waits for 'complete', which never fires while suspended. Measured: before blur 3 sounds; after 900 blurred frames 189 sound objects, all isPlaying, ctx 'suspended'. 400 ms after focus, 46 were playing at once (a burst); it settled to 9 after 3 s. Growth is ~12 sound objects/s, i.e. ~7,000 after 10 minutes in a background window.
findings.suggested_fix: In Audio.play (and updateAmbience creation), return early when `this.sm.context && this.sm.context.state !== 'running'` or when `!this.game.hasFocus`. Alternatively set `audio: { … }` and pause the game loop on blur if that fits the design.

findings.title: Guidance gaps: no arrow after the tutorial, stale zone hints, upgrades never hinted, arrow over an unreachable pad
findings.repro: Casual-model run: node tools/test/review_gameplay_sim.mjs --name e3 --upg greedy --think 1.2 --mag 0.85 --fixmarket --world '<GP-01/02 override>'. Inspect fin.noGuideRuns and the samples' obj/arrow fields in e3_casual.json.
findings.evidence: The first loop is well guided: first coin at 0:27–0:28, fisherman hired at 0:32–0:35. Then there's no arrow until coins ≥ 80: 46 s in the casual run, 20 s for the optimal bot. Only the text '다음 목표: 벌목장 (80 코인)' shows, without saying how to earn (keep emptying the grill the fisherman now fills). The arrow is visible 78–85% of the time. Zone hints last until the player personally sells that product once, so obj_hunt_1 '사슴이나 멧돼지 곁에 서서 잡으세요' stayed up ~150 s and obj_farm_1 ~130 s while the hired worker was already doing it. The strings obj_upgrade, obj_wait and newCustomer are never used, so the bench is never pointed out. When hire_miner is affordable, the arrow bounces over the unreachable pad (GP-01).
findings.suggested_fix: After the tutorial, when no pad is affordable, keep pointing at the next best action (station output with items → shelf → cash pile). End a zone hint after ~60 s or once that zone's worker is hired. Show obj_upgrade once when the first upgrade becomes affordable.

findings.title: Pacing measured; backpack/boots upgrades are a net loss (finishing is faster without them)
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_gameplay_sim.mjs --name e1_greedy --upg greedy --minutes 40 --fixmarket --world '{"pads":{"hire_miner":{"x":778,"y":1889}},"market":{"entry":[[990,2570],[990,1260],[1080,1080]],"exit":[[1080,1080],[990,1260],[990,2570]]}}' ; repeat with --upg none, and with --think 1.2 --mag 0.85 (casual). findings.title: Any exception inside Phaser's game loop freezes the game permanently with no error shown
findings.area: error handling / platform (Phaser RAF loop, index.html error box)
findings.repro: Throw from any update or create (for example save variants R2a/R2b), then watch __FV.game.loop.frame. review_robust_save_fast.mjs reports 'LOOP DEAD: frame counter stuck … for 20 s'.
findings.evidence: In Phaser 3.90, RequestAnimationFrame.step is `function e(i){t.callback(i), t.isRunning && (t.timeOutID = requestAnimationFrame(e))}`. The callback runs before the next frame is requested, so a single throw stops the loop for good. index.html:54 returns early once window.__FV_BOOTED is set (main.js:39 sets it right after `new Phaser.Game`), so no error box is ever shown after boot. Observed: a blank or frozen canvas, no message, and nothing for a non-coder to act on.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a window 'error'/'unhandledrejection' handler active after boot. It should show an in-game or DOM overlay ('문제가 생겼어요 — 새로고침') with a reload button, and optionally a 'start fresh' button that moves the save aside. Optionally wrap Game.update/UI.update bodies in try/catch that logs once and keeps running.

findings.title: Upgrade pads save the previous level's full price as 'paid' → after any reload the next level is discounted by that amount
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_robust_pads.mjs (section A): unlockAll, give coins to exactly 60, stand on up_capacity until level 1, step off, then reload and tap start.
findings.evidence: Progression.upgrade deletes paid['up_capacity'] (line 135) and immediately calls gs.save (line 143). serialize → collectPaid (line 149) re-reads pad.paid, which still equals the full old cost because pad.rearm only runs after delayedCall(500) (line 142). collectPaid never removes entries, so the stale value stays in memory too. Measured: savedPaidRightAfterUpgrade {up_capacity: 60}, and still 60 after stepping off. After reload the level-2 pad has cost 150, paid 60, label '90', with 0 coins. This repeats for every non-final level, so up to 60+150+320+600 (bag) + 90+220+450 (boots) = 1,890 coins of unintended discount for players who close and reopen between upgrades.
findings.suggested_fix: In upgrade(), set pad.paid = 0 (or call pad.rearm synchronously) before gs.save. In collectPaid, delete this.paid[id] when p.paid === 0 and also for maxed pads.

findings.title: Designer balance.js edits can softlock progression: cost 0, a missing cost key, or lowering a cost below a saved partial payment makes a pad that never completes
findings.repro: Serve a modified balance.js via page.route. node tools/test/review_robust_save.mjs only=costZero: hire_fisherman: 0, fresh start, stand on the pad with 50 coins. only=costLowered: zone_farm 200→100 with a save that has progress.paid.zone_farm = 150 and 500 coins; stand on the pad for 300 frames. node tools/test/review_robust_platform.mjs: payDuration 0, a fractional price, autosaveEvery 0.
findings.evidence: costZero: label '0', never completes (doneAfter300FramesOnPad false), so the very first step is blocked. costLowered: paid = min(150,100) = 100, remaining 0, label '0', still not done after 300 frames on the pad with 500 coins. Cause: the only complete() call sits inside `if (this.remaining > 0 && eco.coins > 0)` (UnlockPad.js:133). A missing cost key gives paid = Math.min(0, undefined) = NaN (UnlockPad.js:20), so the label reads 'NaN' and the pad never completes (code inspection). Other edge values: payDuration 0 makes acc NaN after the first chunk (it only completes if coins ≥ remaining in that one frame). A fractional price of 4.5 loses 0.5 coin per collection (31.5 → 31). autosaveEvery 0 writes localStorage every frame (1.0 setItem/frame).
findings.suggested_fix: At the top of UnlockPad.update (and in the constructor), call complete() when `!(this.remaining > 0)` and the pad is active and not maxed. Sanitize balance values on load: cost = Math.max(1, Math.floor(cost) || 1), payDuration ≥ 0.1, autosaveEvery ≥ 1, prices as integers. Add a Korean comment in balance.js that costs must be ≥ 1.

findings.title: In a sandboxed iframe without allow-same-origin the game hangs on 'Loading…' forever (ES module blocked by CORS); with CORS it runs but progress is silently never saved

Case 1: plain static server. Case 2: server adds Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. Case 3: sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin". Case 4: no sandbox.
findings.evidence: Case 1: console.error "Access to script at …/src/main.js from origin 'null' has been blocked by CORS policy". window.__FV is undefined, #fv-loading stays at opacity 1 and #fv-error is never shown (a module fetch failure fires no window 'error'), so it says 'Loading…' forever (iframe_sandbox_scripts_noCORS.jpg). Case 2: boots, plays and hires, audio runs (41 keys, ctx running). localStorage throws SecurityError and is handled, but saving is impossible and the player is not told. Cases 3 and 4 (itch.io-style): fully working, save OK.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the hosting requirement (embed with allow-same-origin, or serve with ACAO). In index.html add a timeout check, e.g. after 15 s if !window.__FV_BOOTED or __FV is undefined, show the existing #fv-error text. When Save.write fails on first use, show a one-time toast ('이 환경에서는 저장되지 않아요').

findings.title: Arrow keys / Space scroll the host page when the game is embedded (keyboard capture disabled)
findings.repro: Same iframe harness, with the host body 3000 px tall. Click into the game iframe, press ArrowDown ×6 and then Space, and read the host page's scrollY.
findings.evidence: Host scrollY went 0→160 (sandbox allow-scripts allow-same-origin) and 0→240 (cross-origin, no sandbox) while the player was steering. Input.attachKeyboard calls kb.addKeys({...}, enableCapture=false, …) (Input.js:18), so Phaser never calls preventDefault on arrow/space keydown, and the scroll chains to the parent page. The PC hint advertises 방향키 (arrow keys) as a control.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass enableCapture = true to addKeys, or call scene.input.keyboard.addCapture('UP,DOWN,LEFT,RIGHT,SPACE').

findings.title: Canvas-renderer fallback (WebGL unavailable or blocklisted, iOS Lockdown Mode) renders no nine-slice UI: coin bar, settings panel and buttons are missing; render ~55 ms/frame
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_robust_platform.mjs only=canvas launches Chromium with --disable-webgl --disable-3d-apis. Phaser.AUTO (main.js:23) falls back to CANVAS.

findings.title: Memory footprint: 60.8 MB decoded audio + ~110 MB of textures (34 MB of them canvas-backed, so also held in CPU memory); TileSprites allocate ~7 MB of unused canvases
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_robust_platform.mjs only=memory. It sums AudioBuffer length×channels×4 over g.cache.audio and texture source w×h×4 over g.textures. The texture inventory is in soak_norender_samples.json → textures.
findings.evidence: Decoded audio is 60.8 MB: bgm_village 25.8 MB (stereo, 44.1 kHz, 77 s), amb_wind 8.1, amb_sea 8.1, bgm_title 7.7, amb_fire 6.7. Textures: 84–88 sources, 28.8 MPx ≈ 110 MB GPU estimate. Canvas textures are 34 MB: fv_ground_0/1024/2048 at 1800×1024, 1800×1024 and 1800×572 (all below 2048 px, OK), fv_floor_* up to 1316×682, and TileSprite canvases 1800×635 + 2×1800×200 that WebGL never uses (Ground.js:45-49). Max texture dimension is 3072 (fx_levelup, 3072×192); GL MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE here is 8192, but 2048-limit devices would reject it. JS heap stays small (~9–12 MB). On 2–3 GB phones and iOS Safari's per-tab limit this is the main crash/reload risk.
findings.suggested_fix: Encode the ambience loops as mono (halves ~23 MB) and bgm as mono or 22 kHz (25.8 → ~6–13 MB). Split fx_levelup and fx_unlock into rows of ≤ 2048 px. Optionally replace the sea and fish TileSprites with tiled images or a shader to avoid the canvases, and drop the baked canvases' CPU copies (convert to image textures after baking).

findings.title: Opaque-origin artifact frame without CORS headers: the normal build cannot load any asset (Phaser loads everything via XHR)
findings.repro: test_deploy.mjs sandbox: wrapper on origin A, <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> on origin B, CSP default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob: ..., no Access-Control-Allow-Origin
findings.evidence: Access to XMLHttpRequest at 'http://127.0.0.1:PORT/assets/characters/manifest.json' from origin 'null' has been blocked by CORS policy (x6 manifests, retried). With ACAO:* (mode sandbox-cors) or allow-same-origin (mode sameorigin) everything PASSES. The host docs say fetch() of files published alongside the page works, so the real host most likely behaves like those passing modes. Verify on first publish anyway.
findings.suggested_fix: No src change needed. If the published artifact shows grey placeholder boxes or hangs on loading, rebuild with `node frost-village/tools/build/build_artifact.mjs --inline --webp`. That writes dist/artifact_inline/: 7 files, 11.5 MB. All assets are embedded in packs/assets_N.js (images as data: URIs, JSON as objects, audio as base64 mp3 decoded with the game's AudioContext), and inline_loader.js re-registers Phaser's json/image/atlas/spritesheet/audio loaders, so there are zero XHRs. Republish it to the same artifact URL. Tested PASS in the strictest emulation (mode sandbox-inline: origin null, localStorage throws, 12 requests, 0 errors, audio unlocked, full loop).

findings.title: First-visit payload ~11.9 MB (64% PNG) - WebP for the big truecolor images saves ~3.1 MB with no visible loss
findings.repro: node frost-village/tools/build/build_artifact.mjs (prints the size table); node frost-village/tools/build/build_artifact.mjs --webp; node frost-village/tools/build/test_deploy.mjs sameorigin
findings.evidence:
Biggest files: props/props_buildings.png 1.79 MB (RGBA 1980x1460), audio/bgm_village.mp3 1.17 MB / .ogg 0.98 MB, lib/phaser.min.js 1.14 MB (0.31 MB gzipped), characters/char_player.png 0.43, audio/amb_sea 0.39, amb_wind 0.37, bgm_title 0.35, char_farmer 0.34. By type: PNG 7.64 MB, one audio set about 2.7 MB, JS 1.28 MB, JSON 0.33 MB.

WebP q90 with lossless alpha, applied only where it saves more than 40%, converts 32 images, 4.29 MB down to 1.18 MB. Examples: props_buildings 1828K to 474K (RMS error 2.5/255), ui_title_bg 349K to 93K, props_nature 284K to 75K, ui_icons 282K to 109K, ground_* about 240K to 70K. The first visit drops from 11.94 to 8.83 MB.

Side-by-side PNG and WebP renders of the title and plaza look identical. The WebP build passed full host emulation with 0 errors. The 11 character atlases are already palette PNGs, and WebP does not help them, so they stay PNG. Decoded memory is about 76 MB of RGBA textures plus about 61 MB of decoded PCM audio.
findings.suggested_fix:
For the artifact, publish the output of `build_artifact.mjs --webp`. It needs python3 and Pillow, and only the dist copy is converted, so assets/ is untouched. For GitHub Pages, the same gain needs the props/ui/ground generators to emit .webp and their manifests to point at it; Phaser loads WebP like PNG, and Safari has supported it since version 14. Lower priority: a custom Phaser build without Matter, Spine and similar modules would roughly halve phaser.min.js.

Note: Pages serves the 32 src modules unbundled, an import waterfall of a few round trips. That is acceptable, or the bundled game.js could be used there too.

findings.title: Lifting the steering finger while another finger is down stops the chief; the second finger never takes over
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_robust_multitouch.mjs dispatches synthetic TouchEvents on the canvas (CDP cannot lift one finger of several): finger 1 drags right, finger 2 lands and drags up, finger 1 lifts, finger 2 keeps moving.
findings.evidence: The joystick correctly stays with finger 1 while finger 2 lands (vx 254, vy 0). After finger 1 lifts: knob hidden, vx 0; after finger 2 moves: still 0. findings.title: If the .ogg files fail to load (host blocks or mis-serves them), all 41 sounds are missing; Phaser does not fall back to the .mp3
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_robust_audio.mjs only=oggBlockedNoFallback: page.route('**/*.ogg', abort).
findings.evidence: cache.audio has 0 keys, missingAudio lists all 41, nothing plays and the only errors are net::ERR_FAILED. The Safari-like path is fine: with canPlayType returning '' for ogg/opus (mp3only), 41/41 load as mp3, 0 ogg requests, and loop buffers decode to exactly the manifest length in Chromium (bgm_village 3,386,816 samples). Untested risk: Safari's decoder may keep the LAME encoder delay (manifest mp3StartPad=1105 samples), which the code ignores, so a ~25 ms gap or click per loop is possible on Safari only.
findings.suggested_fix: In the loader 'loaderror' handler, re-queue the failed audio key with only its .mp3 URL. Optionally apply mp3StartPad as a loop offset when the mp3 variant is in use.

findings.title: iOS: audio can stay silent after an interruption (call, Siri, app switch); the only resume path is the title tap or window focus
findings.area: audio / iOS platform (code inspection; not reproducible in Chromium)
findings.repro: Code inspection. Phaser 3.90 WebAudioSoundManager.unlock removes its body touch/mouse listeners after the first successful resume. Audio.start() (only called on the title tap) resumes only when state === 'suspended', not 'interrupted'. After an iOS interruption, recovery depends on context.resume() from a window focus event, which iOS may refuse outside a user gesture.
findings.evidence: Needs on-device verification. In Chromium the blur→focus path resumed fine (ctx running after focus).
findings.suggested_fix: In the UI scene's pointerdown handler, `const c = game.sound.context; if (c && c.state !== 'running') c.resume();` on every tap.

findings.title: No frame-rate cap: 120 Hz phones run update + render at 120 fps; below 20 fps the game runs in slow motion (dt clamp)
findings.repro: Code: main.js:32 sets `fps: { target: 60, smoothStep: true }` with no limit. Game.update clamps dt to 0.05.
findings.evidence: Headless rendered runs at 2–4 FPS were visibly slow motion: the 12-min rendered soak covered only ~80 s of effective simulation. Logic cost is small (Game update 0.55 ms; full scene-manager update ~1.4 ms on this contended CPU), so 120 Hz mainly costs battery and GPU fill.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `fps: { target: 60, limit: 60 }` (Phaser 3.60+ supports fps.limit).

findings.title: Old or future save versions are silently discarded and then overwritten by the next autosave (no backup or migration)
findings.repro: localStorage save {v:0, coins:999, …} → reload → start.
findings.evidence: Save.load returns null when s.v !== 1 (Save.js:37). The game starts fresh (coins 0, done []), and Save.write always writes v:1 over the same key on the next autosave or pagehide. Any future version bump will wipe every player's progress without warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Before overwriting an unreadable or other-version save, copy it to a backup key once. Add a small migrate(v) hook.

findings.title: Standing on an upgrade pad buys level after level with no pause (standT is not reset on rearm)
findings.repro: node tools/test/review_robust_pads.mjs (section C): unlockAll, give 5000, stand on up_speed.
findings.evidence: Without leaving the pad: level 1 at frame 92, 2 at 165, 3 at 234, 4 at 296. 1,560 coins spent in ~5 s of standing. rearm() resets done/cost/paid/acc but not standT, so draining resumes immediately.
findings.suggested_fix: If the design wants one level per visit, reset this.standT = 0 in rearm(), or require the player to step off first (set a 'needsLeave' flag).

findings.title: touchcancel logs a console.error from Phaser (preventDefault on a non-cancelable event)
findings.repro: During a joystick drag, dispatch CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent type 'touchCancel' (review_robust_input.mjs touch section).
findings.evidence: console.error: "Ignored attempt to cancel a touchcancel event with cancelable=false, for example because scrolling is in progress and cannot be interrupted." No other console errors or warnings appeared in normal boot, the 12-min soaks, resize storms, or the audio and input tests (the only boot request failures were ERR_ABORTED caused by the test harness reloading).
findings.suggested_fix: Harmless. Filter it in any error reporting, or ignore it.

findings.title: Per-frame setDepth on every stacked item triggers a full display-list depth sort every frame (perf headroom)
findings.repro: Code: ItemStack.layout calls it.spr.setDepth(...) for every item each frame. Phaser 3.90's depth setter always calls displayList.queueDepthSort(). Measured with review_robust_soak.mjs and review_robust_drawcalls.mjs.
findings.evidence: There are ~480–900 children with everything unlocked (before the R1 leak). Render-side CPU averaged 3.4–5.9 ms per frame under SwiftShader. Draw calls are only 4–6 per frame and texture uploads are 0 per frame (except ~1.4/frame, 25 kpx, while a pad's cost text changes), so the GPU batching itself is efficient.
findings.suggested_fix: Only call setDepth when the value changes (compare to spr.depth), or give static pad stacks a single depth and use a Container.

findings.title: All audio, including in-game music and ambience (~2.1 MB), is downloaded and decoded before the title screen
findings.repro: src/scenes/Preload.js create(): Assets.queueAssets(this.load) queues all 41 audio files. The title only needs bgm_title and the UI sfx.
findings.evidence: bgm_village.ogg 1.03 MB plus amb_sea/wind/fire.ogg 1.12 MB are 18% of the first-visit bytes, and each is decoded to PCM up front. Assets.queueAssets already accepts opts.musicFilter.
findings.suggested_fix:
Preload.create: `Assets.queueAssets(this.load, { musicFilter: (k) => !/^(bgm_village|amb_)/.test(k) })`.

Title.create (after the UI is up): `Assets.queueAudio(this.load, (k) => /^(bgm_village|amb_)/.test(k)); this.load.once('complete', () => { if (Audio.musicKey) Audio.playMusic(Audio.musicKey); }); this.load.start();`.

Ambience needs no change, because Audio.updateAmbience starts loops as soon as exists(key) is true. Optional: re-encode the ambience as mono Vorbis q2 in tools/audio. Measured: amb_sea 406K to 205K, amb_wind 357K to 205K, amb_fire 355K to 190K. Music at Vorbis q2: bgm_village 1026K to 711K. That saves about 0.95 MB (ogg), pending a listening check.

findings.title: Double-clicking frost-village/index.html (file://) hangs on 'Loading...' with no message
findings.repro: Open file:///home/user/nurient/frost-village/index.html in Chromium (scratch script fileproto/file_test.mjs)
findings.evidence: Console: Access to script at 'file:///.../src/main.js' from origin 'null' has been blocked by CORS policy. #fv-error stays display:none and __FV_BOOTED stays false. The window error listener is registered without capture, and a failed script or module load fires only on the <script> element, so the friendly message never shows.

In index.html, move the error <script> above `<script src="lib/phaser.min.js">` and register it with capture (`window.addEventListener('error', fn, true)`), reading `e.target.src` when e.message is empty. Also add `if (location.protocol === 'file:') show('이 게임은 파일 더블클릭으로는 열리지 않아요. tools/build/README.md의 "내 컴퓨터에서 실행하기"를 따라 주세요.')`.

The artifact page generated by build_artifact.mjs already registers its handler first and with capture. The README explains the local-server way to run the game. The --inline build is the one version that does run by double-click (verified).

findings.title: Artifact republish: no hot-update snapshot, so viewers without storage lose progress when the page is updated
findings.repro: Republish the artifact while a viewer plays in a private window or preview (localStorage throws). The host reloads the page with the new version.
findings.evidence: In the opaque sandbox, localStorage throws SecurityError: the reload step shows coins 12 before and 0 after, which is expected without storage. With storage, autosave every 5 s keeps progress (sameorigin: 12 before, 12 after).
findings.suggested_fix: Optional, in src/main.js: `const hot = window.claude && window.claude.hot; if (hot && hot.snapshot) hot.snapshot(() => (window.__FV && window.__FV.scene ? window.__FV.scene.serialize?.() : null));`. Then, before Save.load(), restore from `hot.data` when it is present. This needs a small serialize() or restore path in Game.js that reuses the Save format. Low priority, because autosave already covers normal viewers.

findings.title: mp3 loops are gapless in Chromium; Safari/iOS (which picks .mp3) unverified and mp3StartPad is unused
findings.repro: Scratch script fileproto/mp3len.mjs: decode both formats with OfflineAudioContext and compare lengths with the manifest's loopSamples
findings.evidence: Chromium decodes each mp3 to exactly loopSamples, for example bgm_village 3386816 and amb_sea 1058432, because it honours the LAME gapless header. So the mp3-only --inline build loops seamlessly in Chrome. mp3StartPad=1105 is in the manifest, but nothing in src reads it. Safari's decoder was not testable here.
findings.suggested_fix: Listen to a loop on an iPhone. If a click or gap is heard, add this to Audio.js after load: for each audio entry with loopSamples where the decoded buffer is longer than loopSamples, copy the frames [mp3StartPad, mp3StartPad + loopSamples) into a new AudioBuffer and replace the cache entry with game.cache.audio.add(key, trimmed).

fix.summary:
Quality pass on Frost Village is done. I reproduced every critical, high and medium finding (or confirmed it in the code) before fixing it.

The village can now be finished by honest play. I ran about 30 bot simulations that steer only through setInput, using the final balance.js. Every run reached hire_hunter with 0 stuck episodes and 0 errors. smoke.mjs passes 23/23 steps with 0 errors.

**Critical gameplay**
- **Miner pad:** hire_miner moved out of the mine-entrance obstacle (now 68% standable and reachable on foot). The miner's home spot moved out too.
- **Customers:** paths now end inside the walkable area. Customers appear at the nearest off-screen point of the entry path, and leaving customers disappear once off-screen. There is a 30 s safety timeout.
- **Partly served customers:** the front customer switches to any stocked food even after a partial order, and pays per item actually received.
- **Raw-item softlock:** a new '버리기' (discard) pad next to the beach campfire throws carried items into the fire. It appears after the first hire and needs a 0.6 s stand. Auto-gather is also skipped while the matching station is full both ways.

**New features**
- **Couriers:** the five post-completion 2nd-worker pads (save IDs unchanged) are now couriers. Each carries its station's output to the counter or trade post, so the village earns on its own.
- **Hints:** a full bag points to where the items can go, or to the discard pad. The backpack upgrade is shown once. Zone lessons end when that zone's worker is hired or after 90 s. Standing still for 3 s shows the next useful action.

**Balance (balance.js and 기획서 §4 table updated)**
- Costs: 30/100/150/350/450/750/850/1250/1500.
- Upgrades are cheaper and stronger: backpack 6→26, costs 40–480; boots up to ×1.6, costs 50–400.
- Customers: spawn every 2.0 s, queue of 10 that turns into the plaza. Shelf limits are now tunable. Bakery 1.1 s, smelter and smokehouse 1.2 s.

**Robustness**
- Corrupted saves are sanitized; a save that still fails is moved aside and the game starts fresh. Saves from other versions are backed up.
- After boot, a crash overlay offers 'Reload' and 'Start over'. Game and UI update loops are guarded.
- balance.js values are checked at start-up; unusable ones are replaced with safe values and a console warning.
- No sounds pile up while the window is blurred. Worker sounds play only when on screen.
- Item flights in progress at reload are no longer lost. Upgrade pads keep no leftover partial payment and need a step-off between levels.
- Arrow and space keys no longer scroll an embedding page. A second finger takes over the joystick.
- Canvas-renderer fallback panels. ogg→mp3 retry. Audio resumes on any tap. Fps capped on 120 Hz screens. Depth set only on change.

**Visual**
- The carried tower sits on the head; it can be switched back with balance `carryOnHead`.
- Canvas renders at device resolution (up to 2x), with a fallback to 1x on weak GPUs.
- The first-loop camera frames net, grill and counter. The market moved inward and the fisherman pad moved right.
- Splash lands on water. Front customer bubble is on top, with a check mark instead of 'x0'.
- Market, trade post and tall stations fade only when the chief is actually behind them (pixel-accurate).
- Soft blurred paths, grounded title art, particle tints that show on snow, frosted previews inside locked zones.
- Rotate overlay for landscape phones, safe-area insets, and small polish (labels, coin spacing, fence posts, banner subtitle, settings icons).

**Deploy**
- Title start frame clamped. Placeholder art now triggers impacts, so the no-CORS sandbox is playable.
- Village music and ambience load after the title. index.html and the artifact page handle script-load failures.
- The artifact build packages only asset folders the game loads: 168 files / 14 MB, versus 242 / 26 MB when it swept in the in-progress villager and emote folders.
- Two fixes touched asset files: fx_levelup/fx_unlock re-packed into grids under 2048 px, and ambience loops re-encoded as mono.

**Not done in this pass:** carrying before the village is complete (GP-05 is only partly addressed), more customer looks (V6), the Pages WebP conversion (DEP-3), and repo-root .nojekyll (DEP-6).

results.note: Reproduced: the pad was inside mine_entrance (standable 0). world.js: hire_miner and hire2_miner moved to P('mine',-0.4,3.6) = (575,1809), now 68% standable and reached on foot. workerHome.miner moved to Z('mine',-0.2,2.2), which is not blocked. All bot sims finish the village.

Reproduced: exit point at y 2660 was below the walkable limit. Market entry/exit paths now end at (990,2200). New customers appear at the off-screen point of the path nearest the plaza. Leaving customers despawn once off-screen after 1.2 s, at the path end (fading if visible), or after a 30 s / bottom-edge safety. 8-min market soak: 29–31 served per minute every minute, at most 3 leaving, at most 6 agents, 0.1 ms/frame.
Same root cause as GP-02, same fix (world.js exit path plus despawn safety nets in Customer 'leave' in Seller.js). Soak stays flat: about 560 display objects and 5–6 agents throughout.

Market.update lets the front customer switch to any stocked food whenever theirs runs out, including after a partial order (the got===0 condition is gone). Customers pay the price of each item actually received (c.value) and carry home what they bought. maxPerType is now balance customers.shelfMax and trade.shelfMax. No stalls in any sim.

Reproduced the full-bag softlock. New TrashPad entity ('버리기', next to the beach campfire, visible after hire_fisherman, 0.6 s stand via balance player.trashDelay): items fly into the fire. Player.update skips auto-gather when that station's input and output are both full (Game.stationBlocked), with a toast instead. The hint arrow points at the discard pad when nothing accepts the carried items. Verified: a bag of 6 raw fish was emptied in 2.6 s, and standing at the net with a full grill no longer fills the bag.

After the village is complete, the hire2_* pads are now couriers (Worker role 'porter', capacity balance workers.porterCapacity 8). They pick up a station's output and stock the counter or trade post. With the player parked away the village earns about 1,170 coins per minute into the cash piles. Carrying before completion is unchanged: it is the core loop in 기획서 §2, and adding porters earlier would change the designer's progression.

Character.carryOffset places the tower on the head (headTop+4) in every direction, with a small per-direction x lean and a ~60 ms glide on turns. This applies to the chief, workers and customers. balance.js player.carryOnHead: false switches back to the chest pose. Verified in S, SE and W screenshots: the face is never covered.

New core/View.js. The canvas is 720k × Hk with k = device px / 720, capped at 2. The Game camera zoom is multiplied by k; UI, Title and Preload cameras use zoom k from the top-left, so layout stays in 720 logical px. Pointer coordinates are divided by k and k is recomputed on resize. At 430×932@3 the canvas is 1296×2810 and HUD text is sharp. A weak-GPU guard drops to 1x if the village runs below 30 fps.

During the first loop the camera frames WORLD.tutorialView (1095,670): net, grill, counter, queue and cash pad together, following the chief only near the edges. The market moved inward to Z(2.0,2.8) with its shelf, cash and queue. hire_fisherman moved to (900,700), so its label is no longer clipped. The 10-person queue turns into the empty plaza.

verify.summary:
Verdict: ship with known issues. Every critical and high finding is really fixed, and no regressions turned up. I found one new bug, the crash card's "Start over" not resetting progress, and fixed it.

The game can now be finished by honest play. A bot steering only through setInput completed the village in 14.4 min, and a bot that only follows the arrow finished in 21 min. Both had 0 stuck episodes and 0 errors.

Fix by fix:
- **Market (GP-02/GP-09):** stays flat over 8 minutes at about 30 customers per minute.
- **Bag softlock (GP-04):** gathering is skipped while the station is full both ways, and the discard pad empties the bag; walking across it keeps the items.
- **Couriers (GP-05):** they earn about 1,100 coins per minute with nobody playing.
- **Saves:** all 27 corrupt-save variants boot.
- **Robustness:** the audio, iframe, Canvas-renderer, resize, multi-touch and pad repros all pass.
- **Deploy:** the artifact builds at 168 files / 14 MB, and all six default deploy modes pass.
- **Smoke test:** passes 23/23 with 0 errors after I lengthened two waits that were too short for the slow software renderer.

**What I fixed myself:**
- **Start over:** it did nothing, because the crashed page's autosave wrote the old game back while the page reloaded. It now starts fresh on both the source page and the artifact. The old save is still kept as `frostVillage.save.v1.bad`.
- **Discard label:** the "버리기" label no longer gets cut off at the screen edge.

**Known issues:**
- In the forest, chopping characters are often hidden behind the pines. The lumberjack in particular is frequently invisible.
- Many customers are the same red villager; this waits on the villager expansion.
- No WebP conversion yet; a first visit downloads about 11.5 MB.
- `.nojekyll` at the repo root is still for the lead.
- The far-camera sound gating (R7) is only partly re-checked: the test harness never moves the camera in headless mode.
- These need a real phone: iOS audio resume, Safari mp3 loops, and whether the sharper 2x canvas holds up. In headless tests the weak-GPU fallback always triggers.

The designer screenshots are in `docs/previews/screens/`. I looked at each one. They cover the title, the fish tower on the head, customers paying, an unlock (payment ring, banner, forest reveal), each zone with its worker, the full overview, and settings.
